Agile

/AJ-ul/ — rhymes with fragile · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone or something that is agile can move quickly, easily, and with good balance.

The agile gymnast flipped across the beam without a single wobble.

Worked Example

The ninja scaled the wall, jumping and leaping with agile movements, never losing balance even on the narrowest ledges.

Agile describes quick movement with excellent balance and control — the combination of speed AND balance is what makes the word precise. Plain 'fast' misses the balance; 'graceful' misses the speed. Agile captures both together.

How Agile Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

nimble

nimble: quick and light in movement

lithe

lithe: gracefully flexible and supple in body

spry

spry: nimble and lively despite old age

Antonyms

sluggish

sluggish: slow-moving and lacking energy or alertness

ungainly

ungainly: awkward and graceless in movement

How Strong Is It? — clumsy → steady → nimble → agile

clumsy vs. agile

clumsy vs. agile: Clumsy is the far opposite of agile: a clumsy mover trips over their own feet, while an agile one glides through quick moves with perfect balance.

steady vs. agile

steady vs. agile: Steady is weaker than agile: a steady mover keeps their balance at a careful pace, while an agile one keeps that balance even at full speed.

nimble vs. agile

nimble vs. agile: Nimble is close to agile but a shade weaker: a nimble person moves quickly and lightly, while agile adds effortless ease and full-body control.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ag

Root — ag: to do, drive, set in motion (from agere) (Latin)

Suffix — -ile

Suffix — -ile: able to, capable of (adjective-forming) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Agile combines Latin agere, 'to set in motion,' with -ile, 'able to': literally 'able to be set in motion' — able to move quickly, easily, and with good balance and control.

Use the root in a new word: agitate

Use the root in a new word: agitate: When you agitate a snow globe, you shake it into motion — the same Latin root agere, 'to set in motion,' that makes an agile dancer so easy to set in motion.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Agile describes quick, easy movement with balance — use it for people and animals moving skillfully. For just speed without balance, 'fast' or 'swift' works; for just flexibility, 'flexible' is better.
